name: Coffeehouse2Home Property Ledger
brief: Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

## Mission
Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

requirements: The suite must provide a single shared Property Ledger where every property has exactly one record containing ownership, address, status, and full history, searchable and updatable by property id, with a test proving the same record is returned and mutated across CRM, flip, rental, and field-ops operations.

The real-estate CRM must track contacts, buyer leads, and seller leads, and must expose a deal pipeline with ordered stages where each deal references a contact and a property-ledger id and tests can move a deal between stages and read the current stage.

Any listing, flip, or rental property must be publishable with showing slots of type private showing or open house, bookable by a buyer with email confirmation, scheduled reminders, and a calendar-sync stub, verified by tests that book, confirm, remind, sync, and list the slot's attendees.

Each property must keep a per-property showing history with buyer feedback entries attached to completed showings, and tests must verify history retrieval by property id and feedback storage with a feedback string plus timestamp.

The flip manager must track acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property, and tests must verify line-item totals roll into the budget, bids are stored per contractor, phase state advances, and job cost is readable per property.

The rental portfolio must manage leases, tenants, a rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders, with tests verifying posted payments update the rent roll, vacancy status flips on lease end, and renewal reminders are generated before lease end.

The field-ops suite must turn work orders raised from any property source (a flip task, a maintenance request, or a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, track crew time sheets that roll into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and track material and supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags, verified by tests for each path.

Work-order hours recorded by crew must be aggregated into both weekly payroll computation and per-property job cost, so a test that logs the same hours observes them in the payroll total and the property job-cost total.

Any showing created on a flip or rental property must create a CRM buyer lead referencing that property, so a test that books a showing on a flip or rental property observes a new buyer lead in the CRM tied to that property ledger id.

Every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders must accumulate on its shared ledger record, so a test performing one action in each domain observes all of them listed in that property's ledger history in chronological order.

All domain records must reference property by the single shared property-ledger id rather than duplicating property attributes, so a test updating a property's address or status observes the new value through every domain view.
edgeCases: Booking a showing slot that is already booked or already has an open-house capacity limit reached must be rejected without creating a duplicate booking, verified by a test asserting the booking count is unchanged.
Booking a showing slot with an invalid slot id or a start time in the past must fail cleanly and leave the slot's booking list untouched.
Creating a showing on a property that is not a listing, flip, or rental must be rejected because showings are only publishable for those property types.

Posting a rent payment that exceeds the amount due or is posted twice for the same lease period must be handled without corrupting the rent roll, verified by a test checking the recorded balance and duplicate detection.
Ending a lease must flip the property to vacant in vacancy tracking while keeping the historical lease and payment records readable.
Creating a work order for a property id that does not exist in the Property Ledger must fail and must not create a crew task or job-cost entry.

Logging overlapping or duplicated crew time-sheet entries for the same crew member, date, and work order must be either merged or rejected deterministically, verified by a test asserting no double counting in payroll or job cost.
Weekly payroll computation with zero overtime hours must produce straight-time-only pay, and with hours above the overtime threshold must apply the overtime multiplier, both verified by tests.
A material or supply line whose quantity drops below its reorder threshold must set the reorder flag, and at exactly the threshold must not set it, verified by boundary tests.

When the email-confirmation or calendar-sync backend is down or offline, booking a showing must still persist the slot booking and mark confirmation and sync as pending for later retry, verified by a test with a stubbed failing backend.
A deal may only move between stages defined in the pipeline; moving to an unknown stage or skipping a required stage must be rejected, verified by a test.
Concurrent booking attempts on the same showing slot must result in exactly one confirmed booking, verified by a concurrency test asserting a single winner.
A showing on a flip or rental property must create exactly one buyer lead per booking and must not create duplicate leads for the same buyer and property, verified by a test.

Updating the single Property Ledger record must be reflected in all domain views without creating a second property record, verified by a test that counts records for a property id before and after an update.
Adding a renovation line item or contractor bid with a negative amount must be rejected, verified by a test.
Lease-renewal reminder generation for a lease already past its end date must not generate a spurious future reminder, verified by a test.
errorHandling: Missing or malformed required input fields (property id, contact fields, slot time, work-order source) must return a validation failure and perform no write.
References to a non-existent property, contact, lease, work order, or slot id must return a not-found failure and must not create partial cross-domain records.

Backend-down or offline status from the email-confirmation or calendar-sync stub must be caught, the booking must be persisted, and the pending confirmation or sync must be recorded for retry rather than failing the whole booking.
Partial writes across domains (for example booking saved but buyer lead not yet created) must be recorded as pending work on the property ledger and retried, never silently dropped.
Time-sheet logging that would double count payroll or job cost must be rejected or merged before payroll aggregation runs, with the conflict surfaced.
Payroll computation that encounters a missing contractor or crew rate must fail for that crew member and report the missing rate rather than computing a wrong amount.
Stage transitions on a deal that reference an undefined pipeline stage must be rejected with the list of valid stages and no stage change persisted.
Rejected operations (duplicate booking, negative amounts, invalid property types for showings) must return an explicit failure message and leave existing records unchanged.
dataFlow: Input (property, contact, slot, work-order, time-sheet, or payment payload) is validated for required fields and referenced ids.
Validation failure returns an explicit error and stops before any persistence.
Valid input is resolved against the single Property Ledger record by property id; unknown property ids fail and stop the flow.
Domain record is created and attached to the property ledger record, appending a ledger history entry.
Cross-domain effects are dispatched (showing to email confirmation/reminder/calendar-sync stub and to a CRM buyer lead; work-order hours to payroll and job cost).
If a cross-domain or backend step fails or is offline, the pending confirmation, sync, or lead is recorded on the ledger for retry without failing the persisted primary record.
Aggregations run over stored records: budget line-item totals, job cost per property, weekly payroll with rates and overtime, rent roll from posted payments.
Reorder flags are computed from supply quantities against thresholds and stored on the supply record.

All reads (showing history with feedback, rent roll, vacancy status, job cost, pipeline, ledger history) are served from the shared ledger and domain stores so a property update is visible everywhere.
negativeConstraints: DO NOT create more than one Property Ledger record per property or duplicate property attributes inside domain records.
DO NOT allow showings on properties that are not listings, flips, or rentals.
DO NOT double-book a showing slot or exceed an open-house capacity.
DO NOT create a buyer lead from a showing without referencing the property ledger id.
DO NOT count the same crew hours twice in payroll or job cost.
DO NOT compute payroll without a known crew or contractor rate.
DO NOT accept negative renovation line-item or contractor-bid amounts.
DO NOT move a deal to a stage that is not defined in the pipeline.
DO NOT generate a lease-renewal reminder for a lease already past its end date.
DO NOT fail a showing booking solely because the email-confirmation or calendar-sync backend is down or offline; persist and mark pending instead.
DO NOT silently drop partial cross-domain writes; record them as pending on the ledger.
DO NOT invent external platforms, dependencies, error codes, users, or features beyond those stated in the brief.
